topology: PC1 reaches the two R3 server LANs through R1 and the R2 ASBR. R1/R2 run point-to-point OSPF area0. R2 has three fully specified static source routes through R3; R3 has an explicit static return route and a diagnostic loopback. Addressing, OSPF, unfiltered initial redistribution, return routing and allowed HTTP are prepared.
implemented: Third ENARSI Layer 3 Technologies lab with accessible counts, six-row addressing/role plan, portable practice/completed variants and current-site permalinks. Both earlier ENARSI labs,39 ENCOR entries, CCNA and Other remain available.

The initial baseline proves actual client replies from both servers and the diagnostic loopback, with three received/installed O E2 routes at metric20 and default tag0. The learner then filters redistribution by exact service/restricted prefix lists and sets tags100/200 while retaining all three original static source routes on R2.

R1 receives two actual tagged external advertisements; the unmatched diagnostic prefix is excluded at the ASBR by the export map implicit deny. Fresh replies from both servers and actual diagnostic No route drops distinguish configured policy from operational export filtering.

R1 FT-IN deny10 matches tag200 and permit100 preserves other eligible routes. The installed restricted route disappears while its received external LSA remains tagged200 and the OSPF adjacency stays Full. New service replies, restricted No route drops and real R2-originated replies prove that the install filter is local to R1.

Four incident repairs cover a source prefix-list denial that withdraws the service LSA, a source retag to201 that misses the local deny200 and leaks traffic, a local match999 that leaks the correctly advertised tag200, and a missing final permit that rejects the service route through implicit deny despite its retained tag100 LSA.

Each repair requires a genuine prior fault and fresh operational traffic. Retag/filter repairs also require new restricted-destination loss after restoration. A native packet-delivery test blocks R2 OSPF datagrams and proves that the updated tag cannot appear remotely until the advertisement is actually delivered.

Fourteen graded tasks combine five live policy/state/save requirements and nine observations. Per-attempt epochs and normal simulator notifications retain synchronous CLI results with a closed guide. Successful outcomes correlate real destination acceptance, router sends and delivered replies; negative outcomes require actual R1 No route drops in the corresponding phase.

The complete prepared HTTP response must traverse the permitted route. Final health validates exact source/export/import policies, tag100/200 and metric20/type2, received versus installed state, original addresses/gateways, installed static sources and return route, working links and HTTP. Final save checks all three routers against startup.

Practice starts0/14; the completed reference provides five live goals without invented traffic, scope or repair evidence. Earned observations survive offline YAML while OSPF databases, routes and transient observer state rebuild. New attempts on the same simulator discard prior incident evidence.
scope: IPv4 IOS static redistribution into OSPF with source prefix filtering and local inbound route-map tag filtering. Multi-ASBR feedback prevention, mutual protocol redistribution, area filtering, PBR and IPv6 are not configured or certified by this lab.

Tags are simulated routing metadata carried with received external advertisements, not VLAN tags or packet-header markings. The local OSPF install filter preserves the received LSA and does not provide a universal interface security policy.

Existing redistribution, OSPF packet delivery, RIB and forwarding engines are unchanged. This update adds catalog content, grading and validation without changing themes, terminal styling, layout, artwork, dependencies or server requirements.
Primary Cisco IOS/IOS XE filtering and redistribution documentation reviewed. No new live CML capture was performed; existing IOS/NX-OS contracts pass in the full regression suite.
